It's the start of another week in DC and beyond that promises all the usual
madness.

In today's '**First Draft** ,' we'll take a look at a confident start to
Maryland Senator **Chris Van Hollen 's** challenge to **Chuck Schumer** of New
York for the position of majority leader. Faced with sneering dismissals from
Schumer's camp, Van Hollen is calling for realism about what the midterms
tsunami really meant: Voters want progressive change, not more of the centrist
same.

We'll also take a look at reality star-turned Transportation Secretary **Sean
Duffy 's** terrible, horrible, no good, very bad couple of days since out-of-
date air traffic control equipment overloaded and led to a nationwide FAA
ground stop, ruining travel for millions and focusing yet more fire on
**Donald Trump** and his terrible, horrible, no good, very bad administration.

Chris Van Hollen thinks there is **" a very open lane"** for him to run in as
he challenges Chuck Schumer for the leadership of Democratic senators and thus
the Senate itself when it changes hands next year.

Schumer, the centrist New Yorker who has been Democratic leader in the Senate
since 2016, has voiced confidence that he will again be elected majority
leader, a post he held between 2021 and 2024. But Van Hollen, the Maryland
progressive, announced his challenge last week, seeking to build on
incumbents' frustration with Schumer and an influx of new senators without
governing loyalties, many elected on progressive platforms by voters
frustrated by Washington inaction.

On Sunday, Van Hollen appeared on ABC's 'This Week.'

Saying **" Schumer oversaw the highly successful Senate Democratic campaign
effort, flipping all those seats blue,"** host Martha Raddatz uncritically
repeated Maine independent Angus King's question this week in support of
Schumer, namely, **" Why would you fire the manager who just won the World
Series?"**

King's not the only Democratic caucus member to make this comparison. **" When
the manager takes you to the World Series, you give him another contract,"**
Ruben Gallego of Arizona
[said](https://x.com/realcrookednews/status/2120254705410707913?s=46) last
week. **" The Brewers just had a record season, and next year is not the time
to change our management,"** Wisconsin's Tammy Baldwin
[said](https://rollcall.com/2026/11/12/van-hollen-announces-bid-for-majority-
leader-but-schumer-says-he-has-the-votes/). **" The same is true in the
Senate."**

Of course, politics isn't a game, and the point of winning elections is to
make policy. The _real_ work hasn't even started.

Managing not to laugh - or to suggest the ALCS or NLCS might be better
comparisons for the midterms - Van Hollen said: **" So, Martha, look, I
respect the work of the DSCC [Democratic Senate Campaign Committee], and I
used to chair the DSCC and the DCCC [Democratic Congressional Campaign
Committee] in the House. But let's be real, this was not a Washington-
orchestrated election around the country. This was the American people rising
up against a lawless president and demanding change."**

He wasn't done.
